items.title: AI Impact On Economy, Russia-Ukraine War Spills Into Poland, No Deal At COP31
items.summary: The AI boom is driving huge investment across the economy, but the buildout is also pushing up prices and adding new pressure to inflation. NATO holds an emergency meeting after three Russian cruise missiles entered Poland, as Warsaw pushes the alliance for more air defenses. Global climate talks ended without an agreement on moving away from fossil fuels, leaving countries further from the targets they set a decade ago.

items.title: Your favorite apple is a cloned ovary – and other apple facts
items.summary: What’s your favorite apple? Whether it’s classic Gala, tart Granny Smith, the crowd-pleasing Honeycrisp or the infamous Red Delicious – before your favorite apple made it to your local orchard or your neighborhood grocery store, it had to be invented – by a scientist . So in this Short Wave episode, we’re going straight to the source. Host Emily Kwong and producer Hannah Chinn dive into how apples are selected, bred and grown, and discuss the discoveries that could change that process. Plus: What’s a spitter?

items.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
items.summary: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.
items.body: A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after 14 hours. Overnight Russian strikes on the village killed 11 people, Ukrainian officials have said. The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday.

items.title: Flights and train services cancelled in Belgium due to strike
items.summary: A series of strikes have hit Belgium in recent months as the prime minister struggles to agree a budget to cut costs.
items.body: Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures. All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair.

items.title: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
items.summary: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.
items.body: Mexican soldiers have detained eight alleged members of a drug cartel whose leader was arrested on Friday, sparking a wave of violence in northern Sinaloa state.

items.title: Trump administration deported US citizen to Mexico, DoJ admits in court
items.summary: Brian Morales García of Texas seeks damages after he was wrongly identified as undocumented in case White House wants dropped The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant. Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.

items.title: ‘Reminds me of home’: why Coming to America is my feelgood movie
items.summary: The latest in our series of writers picking their most rewatched comfort films is an ode to Eddie Murphy’s beloved culture-clash comedy “Good morning, my neighbors!” A young Eddie Murphy shouts from the balcony of a shady apartment building. In the bustling Queens neighborhood, he sticks out like a sore thumb with his foreign accent, tailored blazing jacket and red tie. “Hey, fuck you!” A voice yells from below and Murphy repeats the phrase, believing that it’s a greeting rather than an insult. It’s one of the standout scenes from the film Coming to America, because it’s so absurd but effective in that there is a cultural clash going on here. In Coming to America, Prince Akeem, played by Eddie Murphy, is the sole heir to the throne of Zamunda, a fictitious African country. Instead of having an arranged marriage, Prince Akeem exercises his autonomy and intends to find his own bride somewhere far away from the continent, much to his parents’ chagrin. With the coin-flip and a roll of the personal globe, Akeem and his sidekick Semmi go to America but more specifically Queens because where else would be more fitting to find his bride? While trying to assimilate to the fast pace of New York living, he pursues Lisa, the heiress to a different kind of throne – that of a fast-food business called McDowell’s. The problem is, she’s already engaged to another. Akeem hides his identity as a royal prince and works at her father’s fast-food restaurant to get closer to her. Will Akeem and Lisa fall in love as he cosplays being working class. Will Lisa leave her rich but arrogant fiance? Will their families accept their Lisa and Akeem if they do decide to marry? Spoiler alert: there’s a happy ending. The plot progression is simple but the character development is full of heart and candor.
items.body: “Good morning, my neighbors!” A young Eddie Murphy shouts from the balcony of a shady apartment building. In the bustling Queens neighborhood, he sticks out like a sore thumb with his foreign accent, tailored blazing jacket and red tie.

items.title: More sex, different endings: how fan fiction makes our dreams come true
items.summary: A Harry Potter-inspired novel has earned its author more than £1m in a bidding war. What does this mean for the writers of fan fiction, and the platforms that host their passionate creations? Shortly after this year’s London book fair , rumours began to circulate of a seven-figure book deal for a rewrite of the wildly popular work of Harry Potter fan fiction All the Young Dudes. First published between 2017 and 2018 by user MsKingBean89 on the online platform Archive of Our Own, All the Young Dudes is arguably the most-read work of fan fiction of all time. Now it will be repackaged as a series under the pen name BN King, with the first novel, Wolfboy, due to be published in autumn 2027. This is by no means the first example of fan fiction crossing over into mainstream publishing: the bestselling debut of 2025, Alchemised, also started off as fan fiction based on the Harry Potter series, with some inspiration from The Handmaid’s Tale too. And nearly 15 years earlier, EL James published Fifty Shades of Grey, which began life as Twilight fan fiction before proceeding, in its new guise, to sell millions of copies worldwide.

items.title: Dapper Liam and Noel, experimental Björk, and Bowie ‘cuddling himself’: Rankin reveals his never-before-seen shots of the stars
items.summary: After some satirical experiments with the ‘disgusting’ AI, the photographer has returned to his first love with a book of contact sheets from his celebrity shoots. ‘I wish we could go back and stop everything changing,’ he says “I hate AI,” says Rankin. “A lot of people think I’m an evangelical twat about it, and I’m not. I think it’s disgusting. I think the people who run it are disgusting. They’ve made a massive gamble with humanity and society and culture.” His contempt may surprise anyone who’s familiar with Rankin’s substantial AI output. Ever since the artist Damien Hirst introduced him to the possibilities of generative AI in 2021, the British photographer has been going further down the rabbit hole. “I’m not somebody who likes to be critical about something without actually knowing about it,” he explains. “I’ve gone deep into trying to work it out.”

items.title: Weird lifestyle advice from Gwyneth Paltrow: best podcasts of the week
items.summary: The Hollywood star is joined by celebrity guests as she shares ‘practical tips’. Plus, David Cameron’s deeply personal series about Alzheimer’s The second podcast from her wellness empire is ostensibly centred on Paltrow’s incredibly niche lifestyle advice: where to eat the “best cacio e pepe in Rome”, for example, or “whether it’s weird to use an obsidian gua sha tool on a plane”. In reality, the show is a weekly cosy chat with a showbiz pal (first up, Zoe Saldaña) peppered with a few practical tips – such as how to eat enough protein if you can’t face any more eggs. Rachel Aroesti Widely available, episodes weekly

items.title: Is it true that … we only use 10% of our brains?
items.summary: The idea that we access a fraction of our cognitive potential goes back decades, but does medical science agree? This idea really bugs Dr Mary Spiller , senior lecturer in the University of East London’s Department of Psychology and Human Development, who’s shocked by how prevalent it remains, despite being untrue. Spiller says the myth’s origins can partly be traced to the work of William James, one of the founders of modern psychology, working in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He wrote: “We are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources.”

items.title: Who were 'Churchill's Pirates'? (And how did they outfox Hitler?)
items.summary: They didn't wear uniforms. They sported grubby smocks and bandanas. They manned beaten-up old fishing trawlers that sometimes looked barely fit for sea. And yet members of the Royal Naval Patrol Service – otherwise known as 'Churchill's Pirates' – may well have been the difference between victory and defeat in the Second World War. In this episode, Will Iredale tells Spencer Mizen how a ragtag band of former fishermen and landlubbing conscripts helped stymie Hitler's plans to starve Britain into submission. ----- GO BEYOND THE PODCAST We’ve got a wealth of podcasts on the Second World War at sea available on the HistoryExtra website and app – including an interview with Roger Moorhouse on the brutality of the U-boat campaign. items.title: On this day: 23 November
items.summary: 2019 — The last Sumatran rhinoceros in Malaysia, Imam, dies, making the species officially extinct in the country.
items.body:
2019 — The last Sumatran rhinoceros in Malaysia, Imam, dies, making the species officially extinct in the country.

2018 — Founders of Italian fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana issue an apology following a series of offensive advertisements on social media promoting a fashion show in Shanghai, China, which was canceled.

2015 — Blue Origin's New Shepard space vehicle became the first rocket to successfully fly to space and then return to Earth for a controlled, vertical landing.

2011 — Arab Spring: After 11 months of protests in Yemen, Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh signs a deal to transfer power to the vice president, in exchange for legal immunity.

2010 — Bombardment of Yeonpyeong: North Korean artillery attack kills two civilians and two marines on Yeonpyeong Island, South Korea.
